title: 2018 AMC 12B 21
statement: In \(\triangle ABC\) with side lengths \(AB=13,\) \(AC=12,\) and \(BC=5,\) let \(O\) and \(I\) denote the circumcenter and incenter, respectively. A circle with center \(M\) is tangent to the legs \(AC\) and \(BC\) and to the circumcircle of \(\triangle ABC.\) What is the area of \(\triangle MOI?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(5^2+12^2=13^2,\) the triangle is right-angled at \(C.\) Set \(C=(0,0),\) \(A=(12,0),\) and \(B=(0,5).\) Then \(O\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{AB},\) namely \(O=\left(6,\tfrac52\right),\) with circumradius \(\tfrac{13}{2}.\) The inradius is \(\tfrac{\text{area}}{s}=\tfrac{30}{15}=2,\) so \(I=(2,2).\)

Because \(M\)’s circle is tangent to both legs, \(M=(\rho,\rho).\) Internal tangency to the circumcircle gives \(MO=\tfrac{13}{2}-\rho.\) Setting this equal to \(\sqrt{(\rho-6)^2+\left(\rho-\tfrac52\right)^2}\) and solving gives \(\rho=4,\) so \(M=(4,4).\)

The shoelace formula on \(M=(4,4),\) \(O=\left(6,\tfrac52\right),\) \(I=(2,2)\) gives area \(\tfrac72.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: The triangle is right-angled at \(C;\) put \(C\) at the origin with the legs on the axes
\(O\) is the midpoint of the hypotenuse and \(I=(2,2);\) the circle at \(M=(\rho,\rho)\) is tangent to the circumcircle
